newsitem.title: USA: Tambrands jumps after restructuring news.
newsitem.headline: Tambrands jumps after restructuring news.

text.p: Tambrands Inc. said Wednesday it would close four of nine manufacturing plants in a $46 million restructuring, sending its stock sharply higher.

The White Plains, N.Y.-based maker of Tampax tampons and other feminine hygiene products said it will upgrade and consolidate production in its remaining five factories to combine its separate Americas and International groups into a single, more efficient global organisation.

The company said it plans to close plants in Rutland, Vt., Tours, France, Tipperary, Ireland and St. Petersburg, Russia, but expand facilities in Auburn, Maine, and Havant, England, to become hub locations.
News of the restructuring spurred at least two industry analysts to raise their opinions of the stock.
Tambrands stock was up $2.375 to $44.25 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
The company said the new global structure and plant consolidation will result in a net reduction of about 600 jobs, or 17 percent of Tambrands' worldwide work force.
The restructuring will include the elimination of about 1,100 jobs and the addition of 500 new jobs in the upgraded manufacturing facilities and in marketing and new product development.
As a result of the moves, Tambrands will take a charge of $46 million before tax, or $1 a share after tax, in the third quarter of 1996.
The company said it expected the reorganization to result in annual savings of about $20 million before tax and to be fully phased in by the beginning of 1998.

Tambrands said Edward Fogarty, who joined the company as president and chief executive officer in 1994, will assume the additional position of chairman of the board, succeeding Howard Wentz. Wentz will remain a director.
"In order to accelerate our growth, we must become an even more effective global competitor," said Fogarty.

"If we are to keep winning against much larger companies, we need to be leaner, faster and more efficient in building the Tampax brand with new products, product improvements, education and advertising," he said.

J.P. Morgan analyst Michael Grant raised the stock to a market performer from underperformer because of the restructuring, saying it should boost earnings. Morgan Stanley also raised its rating on the stock, to outperform from neutral.

"We view Tambrands' restructuring positively," Grant said. "Longer term, however, we remain neutral on Tambrands, as it is a one-category company, and we expect the tampon business is likely to remain ultracompetitive for the foreseeable future."
